# National Defense Expenditures (in millions) from Table 4
# FY1933-1941
expenditures = {
    1933: 680,
    1934: 531,
    1935: 689,
    1936: 900,
    1937: 929,
    1938: 1029,
    1939: 1206,
    1940: 1657,
    1941: 6301
}

# Calculate year-to-year log growth rates
# log growth rate = ln(Y_t / Y_{t-1})
import math

log_growth_rates = []
years = sorted(expenditures.keys())
for i in range(1, len(years)):
    y_prev = expenditures[years[i-1]]
    y_curr = expenditures[years[i]]
    log_rate = math.log(y_curr / y_prev)
    log_growth_rates.append(log_rate)
    print(f'{years[i-1]}->{years[i]}: {y_prev} -> {y_curr}, log growth = {log_rate:.6f}')

print(f'\nLog growth rates: {log_growth_rates}')
print(f'Number of growth rates: {len(log_growth_rates)}')
"

# Calculate population standard deviation (pstdev)

print(f'Population standard deviation: {pstdev}')

# Coefficient of variation = pstdev / mean
# Take absolute value since CV is typically positive
cv = abs(pstdev / mean)
print(f'Coefficient of variation: {cv}')

# Round to nearest hundredth
cv_rounded = round(cv, 2)
print(f'Rounded to nearest hundredth: {cv_rounded}')
"
